1380: \begin{theorem}
1381: \label{J-generators}
1382:   Given a bigrassmannian $v=v_{r,s,t,n}$ in type $A_{n-1}$ with $\schubp_v = s_{i^j}$, let
1383: $$
1384: \begin{aligned}
1385: a&:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\\
1386: b&:=\min(i,j).
1387: \end{aligned}
1388: $$
1389: 
1390: Then $J_v$ is generated as an ideal of 
1391: $H^{\star}(G/P_J, {\mathbb Z})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by 
1392: \begin{equation}
1393: \label{generating-set-one}
1394: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}) \}.
1395: \end{equation}
1396: 
1397: Alternatively, $J_v$ is generated by 
1398: \begin{equation}
1399: \label{generating-set-two}
1400: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a) \}.
1401: \end{equation}
1402: \end{theorem}
1403: 
1404: We delay our proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators} until Section~\ref{minconjsection}.
1405: 
1406: \noindent
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.

claims.text: The paper conjectures these two generating sets are minimal; it reports finite verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]

Let \(R\) be a commutative unital ring, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\Lambda_d\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra (\(\Lambda_0=R\)), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge N_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For homogeneous \(m_1,\ldots,m_t\), they generate \(M\) iff their images generate \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Proof: the forward implication is immediate. Conversely, induct on degree \(d\). Modulo \(\Lambda_+M\), a homogeneous \(m\in M_d\) is an \(R\)-linear combination of the \(m_i\) of degree \(d\); the difference lies in \(\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e}\), whose module factors have smaller degree and hence lie in the generated submodule by induction.

Under the preceding hypotheses, a homogeneous generating set of \(M\) is inclusion-minimal iff its image is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning set of \(Q\). Apply the previous claim to every subset obtained by deleting generators.

If \(A\) is a quotient of \(\Lambda\), \(M\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq M\), then \(S\) generates \(M\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(M\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. This follows from surjectivity \(\Lambda\to A\).

Consequently, for the integral \(J_v\), if \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) requires \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators as an abelian group, then each of the two \(N\)-element sets above is inclusion-minimal. This proves the conditional indecomposables reduction.

The stronger condition \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N\) implies the preceding generator-number condition. More generally, for nonzero \(R\), if \(Q\cong R^N\), every \(N\)-element spanning set is minimal: localizing at a maximal ideal and reducing modulo it shows that fewer than \(N\) elements cannot span.

For a finitely generated abelian group \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^r\oplus T\), \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=r+\max_p\dim_{\mathbb F_p}(T/pT)\). Thus torsion can increase the required number of indecomposables; rank alone does not determine it.

Inclusion-minimal spanning sets need not have a ring-independent or even \(\mathbb Z\)-module-independent common cardinality: \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) are both inclusion-minimal generating sets of \(\mathbb Z/6\). Hence the abstract reduction proves inclusion-minimality of the specified sets under \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\), but does not justify a general assertion that all minimal sets have equal size.

For scalar extension defined algebraically by \(\Lambda_R=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\) and \(M_R=M_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\), one has \(M_R/(\Lambda_R)_+M_R\cong Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\); right-exactness suffices, so no flatness is needed. If \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), this becomes \(R^N\), giving minimality over every nonzero \(R\). If \(Q\) has torsion, base change can kill indecomposables, so integral minimality does not automatically transfer.

The stronger freeness statement \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is conjectural in the source, which states that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]

1520: \begin{proposition} 
1521: \label{prop:commalgfact}
1522: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and $\Lambda=\oplus_{n \geq 0}
1523: \Lambda_n$ a graded, connected $R$-algebra, meaning that $\Lambda_0
1524: =R$ and $\Lambda_i \Lambda_j \subset \Lambda_{i+j}$.  Let $M$ be a
1525: graded $\Lambda$-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
1526: $M=\oplus_{n \geq N} M_n$ for some $N \in \ZZ$, and $\Lambda_i M_j
1527: \subset M_{i+j}$.
1528: 
1529: Then a set of homogeneous elements $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ generate $M$ as a $\Lambda$-module
1530: if and only if their images $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ span $M/\Lambda_+ M$ as a $R$-module.
1531: In particular, $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $\Lambda$-generating set with respect to
1532: inclusion for $M$ if and only if $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $R$-spanning
1533: set for $M/\Lambda_+ M$.  
1534: \end{proposition}

1538: symmetric functions with ${\mathbb Z}$ coefficients and setting
1539: $M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$, so that the ${\mathbb Z}$-module $M/\Lambda_{+}M$
1540: is a finitely generated abelian group.
